title: F5-TTS finetune -- T1005 project_name os.path.join absolute-path base-dir bypass
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-43624 (CVSS 8.8 HIGH), affecting
F5-TTS through version 1.1.20.

The finetune Gradio handlers passed a caller-supplied `project_name`
directly to `os.path.join(base, project_name)` across roughly ten
call sites (`save_settings`, `load_settings`, `create_data_project`,
and others), with no validation that the result stayed within the
intended base directory. Because `os.path.join` discards its first
argument entirely when the second is an absolute path, a
`project_name` of `/tmp/EVIL` resolves the join to `/tmp/EVIL` --
completely outside `base` -- letting an unauthenticated attacker create
arbitrary directories with attacker-controlled JSON content at any
filesystem path writable by the server process. The fix's own
before/after test: `project_name="/tmp/F5TTS_PWND_pinyin"` created that
exact directory before the patch, and raises
`ValueError: invalid project_name: '/tmp/F5TTS_PWND_pinyin'` after it.

Detection logic flags a finetune-handler request whose `project_name`
value is an absolute path (starts with `/` or a Windows drive letter)
or contains a `..` traversal segment -- the two shapes the advisory's
own fix (`_safe_project_path()`, adding early rejection of absolute
paths, null bytes, and path separators, plus a `realpath()` containment
check) specifically targets.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor fix (SWivid/F5-TTS, via the merged
PR quoting the vulnerable pattern, the ten affected call sites, and the
before/after PoC verbatim), fixed via the same PR (no release version
number stated beyond the commit).
